name: sol_basics_ac_7
description: Use of tx.origin for authorization/access control instead of msg.sender
question: The source file in `source` contains a function that performs authorization or access-control validation (e.g. an owner/permission check guarding a sensitive action) by comparing `tx.origin` to an expected address, rather than using `msg.sender`, allowing a malicious intermediary contract called by the legitimate authorized account to pass the check and perform the sensitive action on the victim's behalf; this excludes uses of `tx.origin` solely to verify the caller is an EOA via `require(tx.origin == msg.sender)`.
criteria: A function checks `require(tx.origin == owner)` before executing privileged logic such as withdrawing funds or changing ownership
An access-control modifier compares `tx.origin` to a stored admin address to gate a sensitive state-changing function
A transfer or withdrawal function authorizes the caller by checking `if (tx.origin == allowedUser)` instead of `msg.sender`
A function grants a role or permission by validating `tx.origin` against a whitelist mapping rather than `msg.sender`
